project.name: Slurminal
project.description: A Rust and GPUI reimplementation of the Paseo client. Ports the Paseo wire protocol to typed serde structs and speaks the same WebSocket format, so Slurminal works against a real Paseo daemon from the first working build. Divergence from Paseo is a later direction, taken only where the Rust and GPUI stack makes another shape clearly better.

meta.paseo_reference: The Paseo checkout at ../paseo is the protocol authority. packages/protocol is the source of truth; packages/app is the UI reference.
meta.protocol_scale: As counted 2026-09-16: 171 RPC request/response pairs across 281 distinct message-type literals, 15 client capabilities, plus binary terminal and file-transfer frames. This is the size of the port.
meta.stance: Paseo-compatible now, diverge later. Compatibility is a feature until it is a constraint; revisit at v2, not during v1.
meta.terminal_dependency: Terminal panes consume zoid-terminal from Zoid milestone v11.

phases.title: Protocol inventory and compatibility contract
phases.goal: Turn 'port the Paseo protocol' into an enumerated, ordered surface, and write down what compatibility obliges Slurminal to do. No protocol code is written until this phase is done, because the compatibility rules were designed for a TypeScript client and their Rust translation is a decision, not a transcription.

tasks.title: Protocol surface inventory
tasks.goal: Read ../paseo/packages/protocol and produce docs/protocol-inventory.md: every RPC pair, grouped by domain (agent, workspace, project, checkout, terminal, provider, config, schedule, chat, loop, plugin, browser, speech), with a port order and a priority. For each group record whether it is required for a useful client, required for parity, or deferrable. Include the binary frame formats, the capability list, and the handshake. Note where a schema's shape will need care in Rust — unions, optionality, and the append-only rule — rather than discovering it during the port.
success: Every RPC pair in packages/protocol appears in a group
Each group is marked useful, parity, or deferrable
Binary frame formats and the handshake are covered
Schemas that will need Rust modelling care are flagged with the reason
tasks.tests: Documentation task. Cross-check the count against packages/protocol/src/messages.ts.
tasks.changelog: Paseo protocol surface inventoried with port order and priorities

tasks.title: Compatibility contract for a Rust client
tasks.goal: Write docs/compatibility.md translating Paseo's compatibility rules into obligations for Slurminal. The Paseo rules assume Zod and a TypeScript producer: schemas are append-only, new fields optional, new enum values gated behind a capability, and every shim tagged for removal. Slurminal is a consumer, so state its side of that bargain — tolerance for unknown fields and enum values, how it advertises capabilities, how it degrades against an older or newer daemon, and what it does when it meets a message it cannot parse. Serde's default strictness is the hazard here, so the document must name the deviation strategy explicitly.
success: Slurminal's obligations as a consumer are stated, separate from Paseo's as a producer
Unknown-field and unknown-enum handling is decided and justified
Capability advertisement and feature gating are described with an example
The document names what breaks compatibility and what does not
tasks.tests: Documentation task.
tasks.changelog: Compatibility contract for a Rust Paseo client documented

phases.title: Protocol types and transport
phases.goal: Slurminal connects to a real Paseo daemon, completes the handshake, and exchanges typed messages. This is the phase that proves the port is viable.

tasks.title: A paseo-protocol crate with the core envelope types
tasks.goal: Create a crate holding the wire types: the hello handshake, the server_info status payload, the session envelope, ping/pong, and the request/response correlation shape. Follow the compatibility contract for unknown fields and enum values rather than serde defaults. This crate is deliberately separate from the client so the types can be tested against captured Paseo traffic without a live daemon. A conformance test that parses recorded daemon messages from the Paseo checkout is in scope — the types are wrong until they parse real traffic.
success: Envelope, handshake, status, and correlation types exist
Recorded Paseo daemon messages parse successfully
Unknown fields are tolerated and unknown enum values do not abort parsing
The crate has no dependency on the client or any UI
tasks.tests: Conformance tests parsing captured Paseo daemon traffic.
tasks.changelog: paseo-protocol crate with envelope and handshake types verified against real daemon traffic

tasks.title: WebSocket transport with handshake and liveness
tasks.goal: Connect to a daemon over WebSocket, send hello, parse server_info, and maintain the connection. Implement the liveness contract Paseo expects: a ping every ten seconds beginning one interval after connecting, with all inbound activity renewing the lease. Reconnection is not part of this task beyond clean failure — 2.1.3 owns it. Binary frames are recognised and routed, with terminal decoding arriving in 2.2.
success: Slurminal connects to a running Paseo daemon and completes the handshake
Server info is parsed and exposed
The liveness ping is sent on schedule and the connection survives
Binary frames are recognised and routed without corrupting the text stream
tasks.tests: Integration test against a real daemon on a dev port; unit test for the ping schedule.
tasks.changelog: WebSocket transport with handshake, capability advertisement, and liveness ping

tasks.title: Request correlation, subscriptions, and reconnect
tasks.goal: The request/response engine: correlate replies by request id with a timeout, surface rpc_error as a typed failure, and manage subscriptions with the ownership model the daemon expects. Reconnect must re-establish subscriptions and restore state from authoritative fetches rather than assuming the stream continued — Paseo's correctness model is that live streams are for immediacy and fetches are authoritative. Bear in mind the daemon's outbound high-water mark and its 8 MiB cutoff when buffering.
success: Requests correlate to responses and time out with a typed error
rpc_error surfaces as a typed failure, not a parse error
Subscriptions survive reconnect with the state re-fetched authoritatively
Buffer growth is bounded and cannot trip the daemon's cutoff
tasks.tests: Unit tests with a scripted fake daemon covering timeout, error, and reconnect paths.
tasks.changelog: Request correlation, subscription ownership, and authoritative reconnect

tasks.title: Direct, relay, and remote connection targets
tasks.goal: Support the connection targets Paseo users actually have: a direct host and port, the end-to-end encrypted relay, and SSH tunnelling to an already-running daemon. The relay cryptography is Curve25519 plus NaCl box with the daemon's public key transferred at pairing — the relay implementation is in packages/relay and must be matched, not reinvented. SSH only tunnels to a daemon someone else started. Store and manage multiple saved hosts.
success: A direct connection works
A relay connection works against a paired daemon
An SSH tunnel to a running daemon works
Multiple hosts can be saved, selected, and switched between
tasks.tests: Integration tests per transport against real daemons; a relay pairing test.
tasks.security_notes: The relay path carries the daemon's credentials. Match packages/relay exactly rather than approximating; a subtly wrong implementation is either broken or insecure. SSH tunnelling must not store private keys.
tasks.changelog: Direct, relay, and SSH connection targets with saved host management

phases.title: Terminal over the Paseo protocol
phases.goal: Slurminal runs Paseo terminals using the Zoid terminal component, which is the first proof that the component works for a real second consumer.

tasks.title: Terminal binary frame codec
tasks.goal: Decode and encode Paseo's binary terminal frames: the opcode and slot layout, output, input, resize, and snapshot. Paseo serves a snapshot with optional per-row wrap flags gated behind a capability, so advertise that capability and honour the flags rather than assuming a strict schema. Encode resize and input correctly, since Paseo's terminal sizing is last-interacting-client-wins and a client that claims size carelessly steals the PTY from someone else.
success: Output frames decode into terminal input for the Zoid component
Input and resize frames encode correctly
Snapshots restore content and wrap flags reflow on resize
Resize is claimed only on genuine viewport change, not on focus or render
Round-trip tests cover every opcode
tasks.tests: Round-trip codec tests; integration test replaying a recorded terminal session.
tasks.changelog: Paseo terminal binary frame codec with snapshot restore and correct resize ownership

tasks.title: Terminal pane backed by the Zoid component
tasks.goal: A terminal pane in Slurminal that consumes the Zoid terminal component and drives it from Paseo terminal frames instead of a local PTY. The component's PTY layer is not used here — Paseo owns the process — so this is a real test of whether the component's state and surface split is clean enough for a remote byte source. Any change needed goes upstream into zoid-terminal, not into a Slurminal-local fork.
success: An interactive Paseo terminal runs in Slurminal
The pane works with a remote byte source and no local PTY
Any component changes are contributed upstream
Resize and input behave per the frame codec rules
tasks.tests: Manual interactive test against a real daemon.
tasks.changelog: Interactive Paseo terminal pane in Slurminal backed by the Zoid terminal component

tasks.title: Workspace terminal lifecycle and restore
tasks.goal: Terminals belong to workspaces and outlive a client session. Handle creating a terminal, attaching to an existing one with correct restore, keeping a session alive across pane navigation, and detaching without killing the process. Paseo keeps the terminal alive server-side, so Slurminal must not assume it owns the lifetime — closing the pane is not closing the process.
success: Terminals attach to and detach from workspaces correctly
A detached terminal survives and reattaches with restored content
Closing a pane does not kill the server-side process
Navigating away and back preserves scrollback
tasks.tests: Integration test covering attach, detach, reattach, and content restore.
tasks.changelog: Workspace terminal lifecycle with detach, reattach, and content restore

phases.title: Directory replica
phases.goal: Projects, workspaces, and agents replicate correctly with their sequenced cursor model, so the UI has data to show and reconnects do not lose state.

tasks.title: Directory replica model and cursor reconciliation
tasks.goal: Implement the directory replica: three entity types (project, workspace, agent) with independent monotonic sequences sharing one daemon generation, latest projection per entity, tombstones, and full-snapshot fallback when a cursor is missing, expired, or from a previous generation. This mirrors packages/app's runtime/directory-sync and replica-cache, but as a plain Rust model with no React in the way. The daemon retains no event log, so the client must not assume one.
success: Entities replicate from a full snapshot then advance by sequence
A stale or foreign-generation cursor triggers a correct full resync
Tombstones remove entities and a re-appearing entity is handled
The model has no UI dependencies and is unit-testable
tasks.tests: Unit tests with a scripted daemon covering snapshot, delta, tombstone, stale cursor, and generation change.
tasks.changelog: Directory replica with sequenced cursors, tombstones, and generation-aware resync

tasks.title: GPUI binding for the directory replica
tasks.goal: Expose the replica to GPUI views so lists react to changes without copying the store into component state. Paseo's app enforces that its replica cache never observes or mutates the session store, and that accepted cache rows satisfy the same readiness projection as network rows — keep those invariants in the Rust version. Late cache reads must not overwrite state already advanced by live or authoritative data.
success: Views observe replica changes without duplicating state
A late cache read cannot regress newer live data
The binding is testable without rendering
tasks.tests: Unit tests for ordering guards; #[gpui::test] for a subscribed view.
tasks.changelog: GPUI binding over the directory replica with ordering guards

tasks.title: Local persistence of the replica
tasks.goal: Persist accepted replica commits locally so a restart paints immediately and reconciles over the network afterwards. Directory rows and their checkpoint commit in one storage transaction, matching Paseo's rule. Startup and connection must not create demand or install replicas on their own — demand is what drives loading. Choose and document the storage engine rather than defaulting to an embedded database without thinking about it.
success: Replica state survives a restart and paints before the network responds
Rows and checkpoint commit atomically
Startup installs no replicas without demand
The storage choice is documented with reasons
tasks.tests: Unit tests for atomic commit and crash-recovery behaviour.
tasks.changelog: Persistent directory replica with transactional commits and demand-driven loading

phases.title: Agent timeline
phases.goal: Agents stream their output into Slurminal and render it. Timeline correctness is subtle, so the sync rules are implemented deliberately rather than approximated.

tasks.title: Timeline model and sync rules
tasks.goal: Implement the timeline model: epochs, append-only sequence allocation, dedup by sequence, gap detection, compaction, and replacement invalidation. Paseo's rule is that live streams are for immediacy while fetch_agent_timeline_request is authoritative, and catch-up is paged but complete — implement that, do not shortcut it. Turn lifecycle events carry a turn id and snapshots carry an active turn identity, so an old daemon's status is normalised once at the directory boundary rather than maintaining a second activity model.
success: Events append with correct sequence and epoch handling
Gap detection triggers a paged catch-up that completes
Duplicate and out-of-order events are handled without duplication or loss
Compaction and replacement invalidation are implemented
Active turn identity is normalised at the directory boundary, not duplicated
tasks.tests: Extensive unit tests with scripted event streams, including gaps and replays.
tasks.changelog: Agent timeline with epochs, gap detection, paged catch-up, and replacement invalidation

tasks.title: Timeline rendering for streaming output
tasks.goal: Render the timeline: assistant messages with markdown, reasoning, tool calls, and notifications. Tool calls normalise to a single display type, so implement the normalisation rather than rendering provider-specific shapes. Paseo coalesces and paces assistant text because arrival comes in lumps — the same smoothing applies here and is worth implementing early, since retrofitting it later means reworking the render path.
success: Messages, reasoning, and tool calls render correctly
Streaming text is paced so lumps do not appear as jumps
Tool calls render through one normalised display path
Markdown renders with syntax highlighting where the Zoid components support it
tasks.tests: #[gpui::test] rendering assertions against fixture timelines; manual streaming check.
tasks.changelog: Timeline rendering with paced streaming, normalised tool calls, and markdown

tasks.title: Agent lifecycle, streaming status, and attention
tasks.goal: Agent state as Paseo models it: the lifecycle states and their transitions, streaming status, attention-required notifications, and subagent relationships including provider-owned child descriptors. Model the lifecycle as a Rust enum with explicit transitions so an invalid transition is unrepresentable rather than a rendered surprise. Subagent timelines are capability-gated on the daemon side, so advertise the capability to receive them.
success: Lifecycle states and transitions are modelled as an enum with legal transitions only
Status and attention updates render correctly
Subagent descriptors and timelines are received and associated with their parent
An unknown status from a newer daemon degrades rather than panicking
tasks.tests: Unit tests for transition legality; integration test for subagent association.
tasks.changelog: Agent lifecycle, status streaming, attention, and subagent association

phases.title: Core UI: shell, sidebar, workspace, composer
phases.goal: Slurminal becomes usable: a window with a sidebar, workspaces, a timeline, a composer that can create and drive agents, and permission prompts.

tasks.title: Application shell, sidebar, and navigation
tasks.goal: The window shell: sidebar with the project and workspace tree from the directory replica, navigation between workspaces and agents, and the panel layout. The menubar template already provides the app menu and settings integration — build on it rather than replacing it. Start from Paseo's glossary for terminology and its design system for presentation, and take the Zoid design system where the two do not conflict.
success: The sidebar shows projects, workspaces, and agents from the replica
Navigation selects a workspace and its agents
Panel layout is resizable and persisted
Terminology matches the Paseo glossary
tasks.tests: #[gpui::test] for navigation state; manual inspection.
tasks.changelog: Application shell with sidebar, workspace navigation, and persisted panel layout

tasks.title: Composer: create agents and send prompts
tasks.goal: The composer: provider and model selection from the daemon's provider catalog, prompt entry with attachments, and submit. Creation is owned by the daemon across socket lifetimes, so implement it against that model — a request can carry its initial prompt, reconnect resubscribes to the operation, and retries join active work rather than duplicating it. Explicitly requested ids or receipts that an older host cannot honour produce an unsupported error rather than a silent fallback.
success: An agent can be created with a prompt and a chosen provider and model
Reconnect during creation joins the existing operation instead of duplicating it
An unsupported explicit id against an older host errors clearly
The provider catalog is fetched and rendered from the daemon
tasks.tests: Integration tests for create, reconnect-during-create, and the unsupported-id path.
tasks.changelog: Composer with provider selection, prompt submission, and daemon-owned creation handling

tasks.title: Permission requests and approvals
tasks.goal: The permission flow: receive a permission request, present it with enough context to decide, and send the response. Permission prompts are the point where a user can cause the most damage by approving carelessly, so the request's full detail must be visible and the default action must not be approval. Handle a request that resolves while the prompt is open, and a prompt that outlives its request.
success: Permission requests render with full detail of what is being requested
Approval is never the default action
A request resolving while its prompt is open is handled without a stale prompt
Denial is as easy as approval
tasks.tests: Integration tests for the request, resolve-early, and timeout paths.
tasks.security_notes: This surface authorises tool calls that can modify the filesystem and run commands. Never default to approve, always show the full request, and never batch-approve without the user seeing each item.
tasks.changelog: Permission request and approval flow with full request detail and safe defaults

phases.title: Workspace surfaces
phases.goal: The panels that make Slurminal a working environment rather than an agent viewer: files, git, and search.

tasks.title: File explorer and file preview
tasks.goal: Browse a workspace's files through the daemon's directory suggestions capability and preview file contents. Paseo's rule is that directory search is one daemon-owned capability the client must not reimplement or re-filter: a request without a working directory searches the host home for absolute project paths, and one with it returns relative entries. Implement the client side of that contract rather than parsing query syntax locally.
success: The explorer lists a workspace's files
File preview renders text with correct encoding handling
Directory search goes through the daemon capability with no local re-filtering
Large files are handled without hanging the UI
tasks.tests: Integration tests against a real daemon; a large-file test.
tasks.changelog: File explorer and preview backed by the daemon's directory capability

tasks.title: Git status, diff, and checkout operations
tasks.goal: Git status and diff for a workspace, plus the checkout operations the daemon exposes: switch branch, commit, push, pull, merge, and the change-request operations. Respect Paseo's sharing model, which is easy to get wrong: git state is directory-backed and keyed by host and working directory, never by workspace id, so two workspaces on one folder share their git state. Draft comments and comparison state are workspace-owned and must not leak between workspaces on the same folder.
success: Status and diff render and update live
Two workspaces on one folder show identical git state
Workspace-owned draft state does not leak between workspaces
Checkout operations complete and their results are surfaced
tasks.tests: Integration tests covering the two-workspaces-one-folder case explicitly.
tasks.changelog: Git status, diff, and checkout operations with correct directory-versus-workspace state sharing

tasks.title: Workspace creation and worktrees
tasks.goal: Create workspaces, including the git worktree flow, and archive them. Workspace readiness is published before provider startup, so a created workspace can be navigated to before its agent is ready — the client must render that state rather than waiting. Match Paseo on whether a workspace request may carry its initial agent and prompt.
success: Workspaces can be created, including as worktrees
A workspace is navigable before its agent is ready, with the pending state shown
Archiving works and removes the workspace from the active list
Creation reconnects correctly if the socket drops mid-operation
tasks.tests: Integration tests including a mid-creation disconnect.
tasks.changelog: Workspace and worktree creation with pre-readiness navigation and reconnect safety

phases.title: Settings, providers, and remaining surfaces
phases.goal: The surfaces a daily-use client needs that are not the core loop: settings, provider configuration, schedules, and labels.

tasks.title: Settings window and daemon configuration
tasks.goal: A settings window covering host management, daemon configuration, and appearance. Daemon config expresses desired state while the daemon publishes its actual bound endpoint separately, so the UI must not present a config value as a live endpoint. Follow the menubar template's settings pattern and the Zoid design system.
success: Hosts can be added, edited, and removed
Daemon configuration is readable and writable
Desired config is never presented as a live endpoint
Appearance settings apply live
tasks.tests: Integration tests for config read and write; manual walkthrough.
tasks.changelog: Settings window for hosts, daemon configuration, and appearance

tasks.title: Provider and model configuration
tasks.goal: Browse the daemon's provider and model catalog, see per-provider state, and manage custom provider configuration. Provider catalogs arrive with shared thinking sets in a compact encoding and may include references, so decode both the compact and reference forms rather than assuming one. Providers handle their own authentication, so this surface configures them and never handles credentials itself.
success: The provider and model catalog is fetched and rendered
Compact and reference snapshot encodings both decode
Custom provider configuration can be edited
No credential material is read, stored, or logged
tasks.tests: Fixture tests for both snapshot encodings.
tasks.changelog: Provider and model catalog with compact and reference snapshot decoding

tasks.title: Schedules and workspace labels
tasks.goal: Scheduled agents: create, list, inspect, pause, resume, and view logs. Plus workspace labels, which have their own explicitly subscribed sequence separate from the workspace directory sequence — a list request both fetches and grants live updates for that session, and an idle or unsubscribed session receives no label traffic. Implement that subscription model rather than polling.
success: Schedules can be created, listed, paused, resumed, and their logs viewed
Label catalogs subscribe explicitly and receive no traffic when idle
Label assignments follow the workspace directory sequence, not the label sequence
tasks.tests: Integration tests for schedule lifecycle and label subscription behaviour.
tasks.changelog: Scheduled agent management and explicitly subscribed workspace labels

phases.title: Parity hardening and release
phases.goal: Close the gap against a real Paseo daemon, prove it with drift and scale tests, and ship.

release.notes: First Slurminal release: a Rust and GPUI Paseo client speaking the Paseo wire protocol.

tasks.title: Version drift and capability negotiation hardening
tasks.goal: Make version skew a tested property rather than a hope. Slurminal must work against an older daemon missing capabilities it would like, and against a newer daemon emitting messages it does not know. Build a test matrix over recorded traffic from multiple daemon versions and assert that Slurminal degrades cleanly in each case, including telling the user to update the host where a required feature is genuinely absent.
success: Recorded traffic from multiple daemon versions parses without panic
A missing capability produces a clear user-facing message, not a broken view
An unknown message type is ignored safely
The matrix and its recorded fixtures are in the repository
tasks.tests: The drift test matrix itself.
tasks.changelog: Version drift test matrix and capability negotiation hardening

tasks.title: Hundred-agent scale and performance pass
tasks.goal: Slurminal's reason to exist is running many agents at once, so prove it does. Drive a daemon with a large number of agents and workspaces and measure UI responsiveness, memory, and replica reconciliation cost. Find and fix the pathological cases — the usual ones are per-agent subscriptions, unbounded timeline retention, and re-rendering lists on every sequence advance. Record the numbers and wire a regression check into CI.
success: A large agent and workspace population stays responsive
Memory does not grow without bound as timelines advance
Bottlenecks found are fixed and the fix is described
Numbers are recorded and CI checks for regressions
tasks.tests: The scale benchmark itself, run against a daemon under load.
tasks.changelog: Large-scale performance pass with recorded numbers and a CI regression check

tasks.title: Packaging and release
tasks.goal: Ship platform packages for macOS, Windows, and Linux, bundling nothing the user must install separately. Reuse Zoid's packaging fragments where they fit. Document what Slurminal is and is not at this version, including that it targets Paseo protocol compatibility and where that ends.
success: Installable packages exist for all three platforms
Installing requires no separate daemon or runtime install
The README states the compatibility target and its limits
Known gaps against Paseo are listed rather than omitted
tasks.tests: Install each package and connect to a real daemon.
tasks.changelog: Platform installers and release documentation

tasks.title: Divergence review
tasks.goal: Review where Slurminal diverged from Paseo during v1 and decide what to do about each case: keep the divergence, upstream it, or revert to match. The stance was compatibility now and divergence later, so this task is where 'later' gets a date. Produce a document listing every divergence with a decision and a reason, and use it to seed the v2 plan.
success: Every divergence is listed with a decision and reason
Items to upstream are separated from items to keep
The outcome seeds the v2 plan's scope
tasks.tests: Documentation task.
tasks.changelog: Divergence review from Paseo with per-item decisions for v2
